189798:
TESTIMONY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
In Opposition to L.D. 1478
"An Act to Amend the Laws Governing Baitfish Wholesaler's Licenses"
Presented by Representative STROUT of Harrington. Cosponsored by Senator MOORE of Washington and Representatives: BRIDGEO of Augusta, CRAY of Palmyra, SOBOLESKI of Phillips,
THORNE of Carmel, TUELL of East Machias, WHITE of Guilford.
DATE OF HEARING: Monday, April 14, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland Fisheries and
Wildlife Committee. I am Dan Scott, Colonel of the Maine Warden Service at the Department of Inland
Fisheries and Wildlife (IFW), speaking on behalf of the Department in opposition to L.D. 1478.
This bill amends the authorizations and restrictions applying to baitfish wholesaler's licenses. The bill allows a license holder to use the services of up to 2 unlicensed individuals to assist in harvest operations in inland waters of the State as long as the unlicensed individuals remain under the direct supervision of the license holder. The bill removes the restriction that prohibits a license holder from taking or selling suckers, also known as Genus Catostomus, greater than 10 inches in length between April lst and September 30th of each year. Finally, the bill prohibits a license holder from attempting to take from
inland waters live baitfish for resale using drop nets through the ice unless the license holder sufficiently marks the holes in the ice by evergreen boughs or fluorescent biodegradable tape. Allowing a baitfish wholesaler license holder to authorize up to 2 unlicensed individuals to assist in
harvest operations would cause an enforcement issue for warden service. It is unclear as written whether the term "unlicensed" refers to a wholesaler's license, a recreational fishing license, or something else.
Title 12 12551-A subsection 2-B (license required) states that a person may not "engage in taking or
assist in taking live baitfish for resale from inland waters without a valid baitfish wholesaler's license." The proposed language in this bill would contradict current law to allow "unlicensed individuals" to participate in harvest operations that clearly require a wholesaler's license.
Currently, a baitfish wholesaler's license is $26.00. We do not feel that the cost or process of acquiring
the license is an undue burden on individuals wishing to participate in harvest operations.
The department would, however, support modification of language as proposed by this bill in regard to
the marking of holes used with drop nets on inland waters. We do not see a negative impact to holes

being marked with evergreen boughs or fluorescent tape and this language would align with language
that already exists under smelt wholesaler's licenses. We would suggest modifying the bill by removing
section 6 and simply add "evergreen boughs" to Title 12 Section 12551-A 6-B. (3) rather than restate
this paragraph twice.
I would be glad to answer any questions at this time or during the work session.

Testimony In Support of
LD 1478 An Act to Amend the Laws Governing Baitfish Wholesaler's License

Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and distinguished members of the Inland Fisheries and
Wildlife Committee. l am Representative Tiffany Strout from Harrington, representing the towns of Milbridge, Harrington,
Columbia, Columbia Falls, Centen/ille, Addison, Jonesport, Beals, Jonesboro, Roque Bluffs, Whitneyville and Machias in
beautiful Washington County and l am here today to present my bill LD 1478 - An Act to Amend the Laws Governing
Baitfish Who|esaler's License
I am presenting this bill on behalf of my constituent who is active in both trapping and selling baitfish. He brought this law to my attention with specific concern related to three parts of the current law; licensing, sucker fish and the marking of the
bait trap holes.
When this bill was first discussed with the concerns around licensing, l learned about how bait traps are tended and what the opportunity for others to be of assistance with the collection of fish from the traps may look like. In further discussion with the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, there may be a process already in place to address these concerns without legislative action. With this new information I would like to remove the licensing part from this bill to allow time for
further conversations within the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife and the licensing department.
The other two items would remain in the bill. One is to remove the current size limit on sucker fish that is in place from April 15* to September 30"` of each calendar year and would instead make the size of the sucker fish able to be trapped
and sold consistent throughout the year.
The final part of the bill would be to make a modification on how the holes are marked around the traps in the ice. It is important to have the holes marked for the safety of others using the area. Currently evergreen boughs are used as well as fluorescent biodegradable tape. This request is just to remove the addition of the fluorescent biodegradable tape to the
evergreen boughs.
Thank you for your time today. My constituent is here today to provide more details about his experience with trapping bait fish and I believe someone from the department would be able to answer specific questions about the care of the fish and could answer any questions requiring clarification however, am happy to answer any questions l can.
Sincerely,
Tiffany Strout State Representative
